source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Clearly identify the location and name of the facility.
3. Record the date and time of the measurements.
4. Detail the type of industrial emissions (e.g., sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, particulate matter).
5. Document meteorological conditions, including wind speed, wind direction, temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure.
6. Describe the methodology of data collection, including equipment used and any calibration or maintenance performed.
7. Record the exact concentration levels of pollutants in the air, including peaks and averages.
8. Observe and report visible emissions, including color, opacity, and frequency.
9. Include data from continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS), if applicable.
10. Record any malfunctions or downtime of emission control systems.
11. Note any deviations from normal operating conditions that may have caused higher emissions.
12. Include details of any odor or nuisance complaints from the community.
13. Review regulatory limits for the recorded pollutants and compare measured levels
